{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVIgqiM8AAAABXCddjw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm76XzhAl8tE", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm76X", "number": 3, "title": "Bootstrap the Apple Silicon fine-tuning development environment", "body": "## Problem

The repository currently contains collaboration guidance but no runnable development environment. Before experimenting with fine-tuning a local LLM, we need a small, reproducible setup that works on an Apple Silicon MacBook Pro and can be maintained in Git.

## Expected outcome

A developer can clone this repository, follow the README to set up an isolated Python environment for Apple Silicon LLM work, and run a lightweight environment check. The repository is ready for subsequent baseline-evaluation and LoRA fine-tuning Issues without downloading models or running training as part of this bootstrap task.

## Context

- Target environment: Apple Silicon MacBook Pro (Max-series chip; exact chip and unified memory are not yet confirmed).
- Planned experiment: compare a **4B-class Qwen model** before and after LoRA fine-tuning on Python code-generation problems, with held-out evaluation (e.g., MBPP).
- Prefer the **MLX / MLX-LM** ecosystem for native Apple Silicon execution, after confirming compatible package versions during implementation.
- The current `main` branch contains `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, Issue/PR templates, and development/review guidance, but no Python or training scaffold.
- This Issue is for **environment initialization only**. Dataset preparation, baseline evaluation, training, checkpoints, and result comparison will be separate work. Avoid choosing unverified exact model IDs or committing large assets.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Add a minimal Python project/dependency definition with an explicitly supported Python version and a reproducible installation method for Apple Silicon macOS (for example, `pyproject.toml` plus an appropriate lockfile, or an equivalently pinned requirements file). Include only dependencies needed for this initial environment.
- [ ] Add a `.gitignore` that excludes virtual environments, Python caches, model weights/downloads, dataset caches, fine-tuning checkpoints, generated outputs, and local secrets without excluding useful source/configuration files.
- [ ] Add a small **non-training** environment-check command or script that reports relevant Python/platform information, verifies whether required packages can be imported, and gives actionable errors on unsupported or incomplete setups. It must not require a model download or GPU-intensive work.
- [ ] Update the README with the project goal, supported environment, copy-and-run setup steps, and the environment-check command. Preserve and keep working all existing links to the repository's collaboration guidance; remove or revise the outdated claim that only guidance exists.
- [ ] Add only directories and configuration files actually needed for this bootstrap. Keep model downloads, MBPP integration, training commands, evaluation pipelines, and CI out of scope.
- [ ] Verify project metadata and script syntax, exercise any hardware-independent environment-check behavior, and check the documented commands, Markdown links, and whitespace using tools available before merge. Report any Apple Silicon-only checks that could not be executed instead of claiming success.
- [ ] Follow the [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md); use an Issue-linked PR targeting `main`.

## Optional validation

- On a compatible Apple Silicon Mac, run the documented clean-environment install and smoke check and record the Python/macOS/chip information and results. This is useful but is not required when the implementation agent has no access to such hardware.
- Measure import/setup time or inspect memory usage for future planning; neither is necessary for this bootstrap.

## Required post-merge verification

None. No deployment or other merge-triggered verification is part of this initial environment setup.
